dataConfidence.title: Data confidence
dataConfidence.tooltip: Three separate questions, and a profile can answer two of them well and the third badly. How much football these figures rest on; how much of that football the provider recorded in enough detail to count; and how many of the profile's own metrics could actually be computed. A full season of minutes, fully recorded, still leaves the last one open. None of them affects whether this player is ranked or compared — all three affect how much weight the numbers deserve.
dataConfidence.recordedTooltipLabel: Why does this differ from minutes played?

comparison.maturityNote: {total} competitions, of which {established} have played enough of their season for a full-season figure to be possible. {share}% of this population comes from those, and the median player here has {median} minutes.
comparison.maturityEarly: A rank against the rest is a rank against a season that has barely started.

similarityBreakdown.comparedOn: Compared on {shared} of the {expected} features defined for this position ({pct}% coverage). Percentiles are within the same comparison population as the profile above; two players can share a shape at any level, so read the values and not only the distance between them.

radar.title: Intelligence profile
radar.description: Composite scores, measured against comparable players.
radar.tooltip: Each axis is a composite score built from the player's percentiles among comparable players, on a 0–100 scale. The shape shows where they are strong relative to that group — not how good they are. Scores that could not be computed are left off rather than drawn at zero.
radar.notQuality: A score describes statistical fit with a profile among comparable players. It is not player quality.
radar.omitted: Not plotted, because they could not be computed: {scores}.
radar.noneComputed: No intelligence score could be computed for this player.
radar.tooFew: Only {count} scores could be computed, which is too few to draw a profile from.
radar.tooFewOne: Only one score could be computed, which is too few to draw a profile from.

marketChart.title: Market value over time
marketChart.description: How the estimate has moved, oldest first.
marketChart.empty: No valuation history for this player. The market source does not cover everybody, which is an ordinary gap rather than a fault.
marketChart.singlePoint: One valuation only, {value} on {date}. A single point shows no movement.
marketChart.disclaimer: A crowd-sourced estimate from the Transfermarkt dataset. It is not a transfer fee, an asking price, or a valuation anybody has agreed to.
marketChart.ariaLabel: Market value from {first} on {firstDate} to {last} on {lastDate}, across {count} valuations

transfers.title: Transfer history
transfers.empty: No transfers recorded for this player. The market source does not cover everybody, and a player who has not moved has nothing to show either.
transfers.source: From the public Transfermarkt dataset. Fees are as reported there, which is not always what was paid.

presets.fills: Fills the weights below from the role's own definition. Adjust them afterwards — nothing is locked.
presets.cannotScore: This profile cannot be scored against the loaded data.
presets.setToZero: Setting that weight to zero will produce a ranking, against a narrower reading of the role than the one named above.

interpretation.title: Scouting interpretation
interpretation.tooltip: Generated from the figures on this page by fixed rules — a threshold applied to a percentile you can see below. No language model is involved, and nothing here is a judgement the data does not support.
interpretation.description: The numbers below, read. Check any line against the table it came from.
interpretation.strengthsEmpty: No metric ranks in the upper band of this comparison population.
interpretation.watchOutsEmpty: No metric central to this role ranks in the lower band.
